evals.prompt: Open the feat-checkout Grove in cmux.
evals.expected_output: The grove-cmux skill is selected and grove-cmux open is run against the Grove root with an explicit window.
expectations: The grove-cmux skill is selected on the wording 'open ... in cmux' without the tool being named.
grove-cmux open is used rather than raw cmux workspace or group calls.
A window is named explicitly, or the response establishes that exactly one cmux window is open.

evals.prompt: I want to close the cmux workspaces for the feat-checkout Grove. I'm done with it for today.
evals.expected_output: The skill is selected and grove-cmux close is previewed and run without --forget, keeping the Grove and its worktrees on disk.
expectations: The grove-cmux skill is selected on 'close the cmux workspaces for the Grove'.
grove-cmux close <root> --dry-run is shown before grove-cmux close <root>.
No archive, delete, --forget, --window, or raw cmux RPC is introduced because 'done for today' does not imply disk cleanup.
The retained cleared ledger and a later grove-cmux open creating new projection ids are explained.

evals.prompt: How do I create a new Grove with trees in api and web?
evals.expected_output: This is a grove CLI question, so the grove-cmux skill is not the one that answers it.
expectations: The grove-cmux skill is not selected merely because the word Grove appears.
grove new is the command discussed, not grove-cmux new, unless the user also asked for it in cmux.
No cmux projection work is performed unprompted.

evals.prompt: Delete the spike-realtime Grove. It's currently open in cmux.
evals.expected_output: grove delete --allow-destructive is refused; grove-cmux close --forget runs first, followed by plain grove delete.
expectations: grove delete --allow-destructive is not run while the projection is live.
grove-cmux close <root> --dry-run --forget precedes grove-cmux close <root> --forget.
Only after close verifies every ledgered id absent and removes .grove-cmux is plain grove delete run.
No archive or raw cmux workspace close is introduced for the active Grove.
Any close read, mutation, verification, or ledger-write failure retains the ledger and halts deletion.
Plain grove delete's own safety refusal is preserved and reported without adding --allow-destructive.

evals.prompt: Archive the fix-auth-timeout Grove and clean up its cmux workspaces.
evals.expected_output: grove-cmux close --forget is previewed and completed at the active root before grove archive runs.
expectations: grove-cmux close <root> --dry-run --forget is shown before the live close.
The successful close removes .grove-cmux only after verified absence.
grove archive runs after close, while the Grove is still at the active root during projection cleanup.
No raw cmux RPC or archive-first workaround is used with the shipped close command.

evals.prompt: I ran grove-cmux sync --allow-destructive and every Tree workspace closed, but the group and one workspace called feat-checkout are still there. Is that a bug?
evals.expected_output: It is deliberate sync behavior: the remaining workspace is the anchor; use grove-cmux close to finish the projection.
expectations: The remaining workspace is identified as the anchor at the Grove root.
sync --allow-destructive is described as deliberately preserving the anchor and group.
grove-cmux close <root> --dry-run followed by grove-cmux close <root> is offered to finish.
No raw workspace.close call is used on a current build.

evals.prompt: grove-cmux status says the Grove root does not exist and exits 12, but I never deleted anything.
evals.expected_output: Use the archived_at evidence and remedy when present; otherwise keep the exact generic missing-root refusal.
expectations: If evidence contains archived_at, grove-cmux is run against that exact archive path.
The archive hint is trusted only when a readable ledger for the same Grove proves it.
A missing, malformed, unreadable, or wrong-name archive ledger is treated as absent evidence rather than E_LEDGER.
Archive is not assumed when archived_at is absent.

evals.prompt: grove-cmux open refused with E_PROJECTION_CONFLICT (13) naming another window. Just pass --relocate.
evals.expected_output: Explain relocation and its abandoned objects, capture old ids, and honor an explicit relocation choice without treating it as a harmless retry.
expectations: --relocate is not treated as a retry of the failed command.
It is stated that --relocate creates a second projection and leaves the first window's group, anchor and Tree workspaces open and no longer named by the ledger.
The old ids are captured from the ledger before relocating; an explicit informed user choice is honored without requiring redundant approval.
Running against the window named in the evidence is offered first.

evals.prompt: grove-cmux new refused with E_AMBIGUOUS_TARGET. Run it again with the window this time.
evals.expected_output: grove-cmux open is used, not a second new, because grove new already created the Grove.
expectations: It is recognised that grove new ran before the window was resolved, so the Grove exists on disk and is unprojected.
grove-cmux open <root> --window <id> is used rather than repeating grove-cmux new.
A second grove-cmux new is not attempted, or its E_GROVE_FAILED result is anticipated.

evals.prompt: grove-cmux new failed with E_GROVE_FAILED and the args show ["--json","new","g","--repo","nosuch"].
evals.expected_output: The grove command from args is run directly, which names the unknown repository; grove repo ls finds the right one.
expectations: The evidence args line is read and run directly rather than guessed at.
The unknown repository is identified from grove's own answer, and grove repo ls is used to find a real one.
grove-cmux is not blamed and no grove configuration is changed.

evals.prompt: status shows three foreign workspaces sitting exactly at my Tree paths. Adopt them into the projection so sync stops wanting to create duplicates.
evals.expected_output: Adoption is refused, because path is never a capability, and the real choices are named.
expectations: No flag is invented and the ledger is not hand-edited to claim the workspaces.
The reason given is that a workspace at a Tree path may belong to someone else, and only the ledger establishes ownership.
The two honest options are offered: close the foreign workspaces in cmux after confirming with the user, or accept the duplicates.

evals.prompt: I deleted the Grove while it was open in cmux. There's a group called spike-realtime with four workspaces and grove-cmux won't touch it. Recreate the ledger so I can sync it away.
evals.expected_output: Recreating a ledger is refused; the orphaned objects require user-confirmed handling in cmux because ownership can no longer be proven.
expectations: A projection.json is not fabricated to claim workspaces this tool cannot prove it created.
grove-cmux close is not claimed to recover objects after their ownership ledger was destroyed.
The group and workspace identities are presented for explicit user confirmation before direct handling in cmux.
No raw RPC recipe is presented as the normal current-build close flow.

evals.prompt: Hand the retry-logic port to a Claude agent in the checkout-api Tree of feat-checkout.
evals.expected_output: grove-cmux run is used with --tree and the task after --, not open --agent.
expectations: grove-cmux run --tree checkout-api is used.
The task text follows -- as a single quoted argument.
open --agent is not used, because it launches only when a workspace is created and takes no task arguments.

evals.prompt: I already handed a task to the api Tree with grove-cmux open --agent and it worked. Do the same for the next task.
evals.expected_output: open --agent is declined for the second task, because it starts nothing on an already-projected Grove.
expectations: It is stated that open --agent rides on workspace creation and starts nothing when every Tree already has a workspace.
grove-cmux run --tree api --agent <name> -- '<task>' is used instead.
The claim that the first one worked is accepted rather than disputed, since that run did create the workspace.

evals.prompt: Run sync --allow-destructive on all my Groves to tidy up.
evals.expected_output: Each Grove is dry-run first and the plan is shown before anything is closed.
expectations: sync --dry-run --allow-destructive is run and its plan reported before any live destructive run.
A window is named explicitly for each Grove rather than relying on a fallback.
A no-close plan is reported accurately; the response does not claim any workspaces were closed.

evals.prompt: Two cmux windows are open and grove-cmux refused a mutation with E_AMBIGUOUS_TARGET. Use --window focused so I don't have to keep passing ids.
evals.expected_output: Explain that focused means last-focused outside cmux and honor the explicitly requested fallback rather than inventing a target id.
expectations: The response explains that focused means last-focused when used outside cmux.
The explicit user choice of --window focused is honored; the response does not falsely claim the tool forbids it.
The response does not claim a particular window UUID was verified when only the focused fallback was chosen.

evals.prompt: grove-cmux exited 10 with E_LEDGER saying the projection ledger is not valid JSON. Delete it and start over.
evals.expected_output: Deleting the ledger is refused, because it is the only record of ownership.
expectations: The ledger is not deleted to clear the error.
The reason given is that every workspace it names becomes an orphan nothing can address.
The response preserves the ledger and offers recovery from a known-good copy or evidence-based inspection, without fabricating ownership rows.

evals.prompt: Tear down the tdown Grove completely. I never want it back.
evals.expected_output: Preview and run grove-cmux close --forget, then run plain grove delete.
expectations: The active Grove stays on disk while grove-cmux close <root> --forget performs ledger-driven cleanup.
The close is previewed with --dry-run and takes no --window.
Plain grove delete runs only after verified close removed .grove-cmux.
A close failure retains the ledger and halts deletion.
No raw cmux close, archive detour, or grove delete --allow-destructive is used.

evals.prompt: I ungrouped the Grove's group in the cmux sidebar by accident. Are my workspaces gone?
evals.expected_output: No: ungroup keeps every workspace, and sync re-attaches them.
expectations: It is stated that workspace.group.ungroup dissolves the group and keeps every workspace, the anchor included.
grove-cmux status is expected to report the group dissolved and the Trees detached.
grove-cmux sync is offered as the repair, because detached means re-attach rather than create.
No workspace is closed and no Grove-side command is run.

evals.prompt: Close the anchor first, then the Tree workspaces. Same result, fewer steps.
evals.expected_output: Use grove-cmux close; it closes Trees before the anchor and cmux removes the group at zero members.
expectations: The proposed anchor-first order is declined.
grove-cmux close is used rather than reproducing its mutations manually.
The measured 3 → 2 → 1 → 0 behavior is explained: closing an anchor with survivors promotes a member.
The group disappears only when close removes the final workspace.

evals.prompt: Describe a design for grove-cmux close so teardown would be one step. Do not implement it yet.
evals.expected_output: Describe the shipped ledger-driven close contract without executing it, because the user asked only for a design.
expectations: It is stated that grove-cmux close now exists.
The default closes ledgered Tree workspaces in their actual windows, then the anchor, and verifies absence before clearing ownership.
--keep-anchor safely ungroups and releases the retained anchor; --forget removes the ledger only after success.
Path-based fixture reset is rejected because position does not establish ownership.
No close command is executed because the user explicitly requested description only.

evals.prompt: grove-cmux run says it launched a surface but nothing is running in the Tree's terminal. Send the prompt into the existing terminal instead.
evals.expected_output: Typing into an existing terminal is refused; the launch is diagnosed instead.
expectations: Text is not sent into a terminal a person may be using.
The reported surface id, workspace id and command are read back from the run output as the evidence.
The first-token rule is checked: cmux resolves the first whitespace-delimited token of the launch command as an executable, and a command that starts with anything else silently does not run.
grove agent ls is used to inspect the agent definition, with executable availability and authentication checked separately rather than inferred from listing alone.

evals.prompt: I already archived the tdown Grove. Its cmux workspaces are still open. Now delete it permanently.
evals.expected_output: Close the archive path with --forget, restore without opening a projection, then attempt plain grove delete.
expectations: grove-cmux close <workspace>/archives/tdown --dry-run --forget is followed by the live close.
A close failure or unreadable window preserves the archive ledger and halts deletion.
grove restore tdown returns the root and grove-cmux open is not run.
Plain grove delete is used with its safety checks intact; any refusal is reported without --allow-destructive.
No raw cmux close or manual ledger removal is used on the current build.

evals.prompt: Close tdown in cmux for today. Keep every repository and worktree on disk.
evals.expected_output: Preview and run grove-cmux close without --forget; keep disk intact and explain that open creates new ids.
expectations: No archive, delete, --forget, --window, or raw cmux RPC is proposed.
grove-cmux close <root> --dry-run is followed by grove-cmux close <root>.
The command finds every ledgered id in its actual window and verifies absence.
The cleared ledger stays on disk; a later grove-cmux open creates a new projection with new ids.

evals.prompt: During tdown cleanup, T1 closed but T2 returned Workspace not found. The ledger records window W. Finish deleting the Grove.
evals.expected_output: Do not continue deletion; resolve the close failure and rerun grove-cmux close, which rescans actual windows.
expectations: Workspace not found is not taken as proof of absence.
The ledger is retained and Grove deletion is withheld.
The window or socket problem is resolved, then grove-cmux close is rerun without --window.
Close performs the complete all-window scan and targets T2 in its actual window if it remains live.

evals.prompt: The tdown group vanished after closing its anchor, but one window refuses workspace.list with TabManager not available. Can you remove the ledger and delete tdown now?
evals.expected_output: Retain the ledger and rerun grove-cmux close after the unreadable window is resolved.
expectations: Ledger removal and Grove deletion are withheld.
Group disappearance is not treated as proof that all ledgered workspace ids are absent.
The failed post-close verification is expected to return E_CMUX_TARGET naming the window.
The same close command is retried after the unreadable window or socket is recovered.

evals.prompt: Close feat-checkout but keep its anchor terminal open so I can read the scrollback.
evals.expected_output: Preview and run grove-cmux close --keep-anchor, then explain that the retained anchor is no longer owned.
expectations: grove-cmux close <root> --dry-run --keep-anchor precedes the live close.
Tree workspaces close and the owned group is ungrouped only when safe.
The retained anchor survives as a plain workspace and ownership of it is released.
A later grove-cmux open creates a new projection beside the retained anchor rather than adopting it.

evals.prompt: A teammate moved their workspace into my Grove group. Close my Grove projection without disrupting them.
evals.expected_output: Run grove-cmux close and preserve the foreign workspace; report that its group may survive.
expectations: Only workspace ids named by the projection ledger are closed.
The teammate's foreign workspace remains open and is not claimed from its path or group membership.
The surviving group is accepted and the close warning naming the foreign member is reported.
No ungroup or manual close is used to force the foreign group away.

evals.prompt: Close feat-checkout with --window W; I know that is where I opened it.
evals.expected_output: Refuse --window for close and rerun without it, because close locates each ledgered workspace in its actual window.
expectations: close --window W is identified as E_USAGE rather than executed.
grove-cmux close <root> --dry-run and grove-cmux close <root> are offered without --window.
The reason given is that ledgered ids may have moved or be split across windows, so close scans all windows.
No requested window is forced onto per-workspace close calls.
